title: Turbocharger Component Locations
introduction:
I use this drawing as a map of the EcoBoost’s boost-control hardware. Match each numbered pointer to the adjacent table; the transparent engine parts help reveal components that would otherwise hide behind the surrounding hardware.

The turbocharger uses exhaust energy to drive a compressor that pressurizes incoming fresh air. Think of the turbine and compressor as partners sharing a shaft, with separate gas passages—not an exhaust cocktail being poured into the intake. The wastegate regulates turbine energy by allowing some exhaust to bypass it. The intake-side bypass valve works on compressed fresh air instead, so those bypass functions belong to different sides of the system.

Keep the wastegate actuator and wastegate control valve solenoid distinct when identifying parts: the drawing labels separate pieces of the control hardware. This is a component-location reference for the engine named below, not a hose-routing, testing or replacement procedure.

edits.why: The engine label defines the drawing’s applicability. Use the numbered illustration with its table to identify the hardware without applying this arrangement to a naturally aspirated engine.
